stageMeta.title: Productized
headerComment: # Stage 11 — Productized
# L11 = L10 + product configuration.  Every plugin from Stage 06 is still
# here — sandbox, approval, FS, shell, search, persistence, resume — plus
# the accumulated closures of L7 (stateful tasks), L8 (multi-agent),
# L9 (workflow + context management) and L10 (operability), and finally
# the product-config seam, now with real providers:
#   dsh-settings-file      file-backed settings provider: one user-editable
#                          settings.yaml whose per-namespace sections layer
#                          OVER each plugin's composition base — edit the
#                          file and watchers re-resolve live (watch: true)
#   dsh-credentials-local  file-backed credential provider: the live
#                          process environment layered over a managed
#                          .credentials.yaml document
# Architecture concept: composition → product config.  Until L10 the model
# route, the API-key reference and the sandbox/approval mode were frozen
# into this file — changing them meant editing the composition.  With the
# two providers mounted, dsh-llm-pi-ai's already-wired consumers go live:
# installSettingsSection() turns its `llm-pi-ai` namespace (providers,
# models, retryPolicy) into a hot-swappable user document, and every model
# request resolves `apiKeyEnv: QA_API_KEY` through ctx.credentials
# (per-operation resolution, so a rotated secret reaches the very next
# request without restarting any plugin).
# The abstract seams (dsh-settings, dsh-credentials) stay DISABLED under
# the same rule as dsh-jobs and dsh-compaction below: the provider extends
# the abstract class and registers the same service name, and cordis
# registers one service per name — mounting both fails the boot.
# Still open at 0.1.0-rc.6: the roadmap's preset / bundle / HMR have no
# standalone npm packages in this release — they live inside the dsh CLI's
# `dsh-base` profile bundle.  What this stage closes is the product-config
# seam itself: settings and credentials are real services now.
# The persona is frozen (byte-for-byte identical to L4/L5/L6) so the whole
# L4→L11 progression remains a single-variable experiment.
# Second L11 closure — human entry points + product UX:
#   dsh-commands + dsh-command-compact/goal/feedback  slash-command surface
#   dsh-tool-ask-user    activates the L7 user-questions seam for the model
#   dsh-session-title (+ first-prompt-llm)  automatic session titles
#   dsh-agent-default-model  process-wide default route, settings-layered
#   dsh-persona / dsh-agent-tool-presentation  DISABLED: agent-preset-only rows
#                        (deployment-level equivalents: system-prompt persona,
#                        dsh-tools mode config)

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal
comments: # Storage provider chain for the workspace registry: the hub (ctx.storage)
# names backends, the sqlite backend serves the kv facet, and the domain
# data form mounts schema-validated KV domains and provides
# ctx.storageDomain — the service dsh-workspace injects.  sqlite `path`
# and the domain `backend` route are both REQUIRED keys; defaults are
# taken everywhere else (journalMode wal, no per-domain routes).

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials
comments: # The providers that make the seam real.  Both follow the persistence
# convention (root: ./sessions): an explicit `path` inside the disposable
# workspace instead of the $DSH_HOME default, and watch: true (default) so
# an external edit re-resolves live.  dsh-home-paths and dsh-atomic-write
# are libraries these providers import, not plugins — nothing to mount.
